request:
I run a small provisions shop in Madina and I want to keep my price list on the computer instead of in my notebook. I want to add the things I sell with their prices. I want to see everything I sell, and look up the price of one thing. Sometimes I stop selling something, so I want to take it off the list.

The client's answers to your questions:
Q: When a price goes up or down, do you want to change it on the list, and should the old price be kept so you can see what it used to be?
A: Yes, prices change all the time, especially sugar, rice and oil. I need to change the price of an item.
Q: Do some things come in different sizes or ways of selling (for example a single sachet and a full box), each with its own price?
A: No preference: you decide.
Q: When you look up a price, will you type the full name exactly, or do you want to type part of a name (like "milk") and see everything that matches?
A: No preference: you decide.

Where the client has no preference or did not answer, choose the simplest option and add nothing they did not ask for (no logins, PINs or extra required fields).

The client also wants: Every item has a category I choose, like Drinks, Toiletries or Foodstuff, and I want to see only one category at a time.
summary:
I've built your price list in `app.py`. All 5 test groups pass. The list is saved in a file called `shop.db` in the project folder, so it stays there after the computer is switched off.

**What you can do with it:**
- **Add an item:** `POST /items` with a name, a price and a category (for example Drinks, Toiletries or Foodstuff). You can type any category you like.
- **See everything you sell:** `GET /items`, sorted by name.
- **See one category only:** `GET /items?category=Drinks`. Capital letters don't matter, so "drinks" works too.
- **Look up the price of one item:** `GET /items/{id}`. Every item gets an ID number when you add it, and you look items up by that number, not by typing the name.
- **Change a price:** `PATCH /items/{id}` with the new price. The new price replaces the old one; it doesn't keep a record of what the item used to cost.
- **Take an item off the list:** `DELETE /items/{id}`.

**What it refuses:**
- An item with no name or no category.
- A price of zero or less.
- A second item with the same name as one already on the list (capital letters don't count, so "water" and "Water" are the same).
- Looking up, changing or removing an ID that doesn't exist.

**Choices I made where you had no preference:**
- Each item has one price only. If you sell something in two ways (for example a single sachet and a full box), add them as two separate items.
- You can only change an item's price. To fix a misspelled name or the wrong category, remove the item and add it again.
